title: Spotfall Surge Safety Margin Provisioner — private VPC workbook
body:
Goal:
Provide a small, pragmatic workbook for sizing safety-margin (spare) GPUs and eviction strategies for customers who run Private/VPC deployments that mix reserved and spot-like capacity (cloud preemptible or partner-sourced spare nodes). This is intentionally opinionated: give SRE/infra teams a default and a way to tune it per workload.

Context and motivation:
- We are seeing increasing requests to support hybrid Private fleets: dedicated reserved racks + opportunistic spot pools for burst.
- Customers expect consistent latency SLOs (p50/p95/p99). When spotfall (mass preemption) happens we need clear guardrails to keep critical traffic within SLOs, and procurement guidance for how many spares to buy/hold on prem.
- Existing capacity sheets focus on steady-state tiling; this workbook focuses on transient risk (evictions) and how to size a small, rotating safety pool.

Quick summary (defaults):
- Target reliability during spotfall: keep p95 latency under 2× baseline and p99 under 3× for up to 30 minutes of degraded throughput while auto-failover happens.
- Recommended minimum safety margin: floor(peak_reserved_qps * 0.12) GPUs per region (12% of peak reserved footprint).
- Rotating spare ratio for on-prem: 1 spare per 8 production GPUs (12.5%) with a minimum of 2 spares per region.
- Eviction priority: batch/burst lanes -> low-priority models -> canary routes -> core routes.

Primary inputs (sheet columns / user-provided cells):
- Region (string)
- Model family (e.g., redwood-70b-quantized)
- Baseline GPUs (reserved, integer)
- Peak burst GPUs (opportunistic expected, integer)
- Typical utilization (avg GPU util, percent)
- Target p99 latency SLO (ms)
- Token throughput per GPU at 8k context (tokens/s)
- Mean request tokens per call
- Acceptable degraded capacity window (minutes) — default 30

Supporting computed fields (formulas expressed in plain text):
- Baseline_tokens_per_sec = Baseline_GPUs * tokens_per_gpu
- Peak_total_capacity = Baseline_GPUs + Peak_burst_GPUs
- Safety_floor = ceil(Baseline_GPUs * 0.12) // default 12% safety margin
- Minimum_rotating_spares = max(2, ceil(Baseline_GPUs / 8))
- Eviction_buffer_tokens = Safety_floor * tokens_per_gpu
- Reorder_point (procurement) = Baseline_GPUs + Minimum_rotating_spares (for procurement planning)

Example scenario (region: eu-west-1, model: rw-70b-q4f):
- Baseline GPUs: 80 (A100 equivalent)
- Peak opportunistic: 40
- tokens_per_gpu: 2200 (tokens/s at target sequence distribution)
- Baseline_tokens_per_sec = 80 * 2200 = 176k t/s
- Safety_floor = ceil(80 * 0.12) = 10 GPUs
- Minimum_rotating_spares = max(2, ceil(80/8)) = 10 GPUs
- Eviction_buffer_tokens = 10 * 2200 = 22k t/s (sustains ~12.5% of baseline)
- Notes: this matches the 12% rule and gives an actionable spare count (10) which is the same as rotating spare ratio; procurement teams should plan for +10 GPUs in the BOM for eu-west-1.

Spotfall stress test guidance (runbook snippets):
1) Detection: sudden >40% drop in opportunistic pool within rolling 1m window OR >10% of reserved nodes show degraded health. Trigger incident playbook. (Metric: node_active_count.opportunistic / node_expected.opportunistic)
2) Immediate mitigation (0–2m): throttle or shed batch lanes; redirect low-priority routes to region fallback; enable prefix cache serving for heavy recurrent prompts.
3) Short-term mitigation (2–15m): spin up pre-provisioned safety_pool (10 GPUs) using reserved spares or cross-region failover; reduce concurrency for non-critical routes.
4) Recovery (15–60m): re-balance KV caches, warm new nodes, progressively scale back failures. Post-incident: run allocation analysis.

Procurement / BOM notes (how to think about buys):
- For mixed clouds / on-prem: prefer smaller increments when buying spares if lead times are short (e.g., 4–8 GPU units). If procurement lead time > 8 weeks, increase safety_floor by 1.5×.
- Suggested SKU split for on-prem safety pool: match primary prod SKU; if heterogeneous, 70% matching primary + 30% flexible (cheaper, lower vram) that can host low-priority lanes.
- Replacement rotation cadence: swap 1/12 of rotating spares every month (annual refresh ~100% over 12 months) to maintain warranty and reduce correlated failures.

Cost example (back-of-envelope):
- Assume A100-equivalent spot price saving = 0.5× on reserved cost. If safety_pool = 10 GPUs at $X/month reserved-equivalent, cost of holding spares = 10 * $X. Compare this to estimated outage cost if spotfall causes SLA misses (use customer-specific revenue numbers).

Edge cases and tuning knobs:
- Very latency-sensitive workloads (p99 < 100ms): raise safety_floor to 20–25% and require cross-region hot-standby.
- Small clusters (baseline <= 6 GPUs): use a minimum safety_floor of 1 spare, consider cold-start buffer (longer warmup).
- Heavily bursty workloads (peak_opportunistic > baseline): prefer larger rotating spares and preprovisioned warm nodes (warm VMs with cached model weights).

Open questions / TODOs (actionable):
- [ ] Validate tokens_per_gpu numbers across more model families (Evelyn to run perf sweep). Ticket INFRA-2345 assigned.
- [ ] Add automatic knob to tie safety_floor % to historical preemption volatility per region. (ML: Samir)
- [ ] Add cost-impact tab that models per-hour outage costs vs hold-cost. (Marco)

References and links:
- Performance bench notes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmarks/tree/main/70b
- Slack discussion: #private-deploy-spots (thread ts:16101234)
- Related Linear: INFRA-2345 (eviction policy proposal)

Micro-checklist for HQs / SRE handoff:
- Finalize tokens_per_gpu numbers for chosen SKUs (bench runs + warmup measured)
- Confirm procurement lead times per region (APAC tends to be longer; bump safety_floor +50% if >8 weeks)
- Bake eviction-policy mapping into deployment manifest (suggested rollout in infra PR #789)

Notes to self (rough):
- This is a practical, intentionally conservative heuristic. We should pair with an automated historical volatility calc to make it more precise later.
- Keep minimum_rotating_spares aligned with on-call ops playbooks so spin-up is a single decision ("enable safety-pool region X").

Commentary on uniqueness: unlike our other BOM / tiling sheets this focuses on transient risk (preemption) and operational playbooks rather than long-run purchase curves. It should be useful to both product SRE and procurement teams when sizing early customer Private fleets.

(End of workbook - paste into a Google Sheet and wire the computed fields to the named input cells above.)
